title: Choose the Products workspace direction
question: Each option supports the same stockroom tasks. Choose the visual system that best fits how shop teams work.

options.label: Stockroom bin-card system
options.lineage: warehouse bin cards and receiving labels
options.thesis: A live shelf of precise inventory cards, built for scanning while standing in the stockroom.
options.viewport: A dark utility rail anchors the page while large product rows line up like labeled bin cards; search and Add product live at the top edge.
options.risk: Requires disciplined density so it stays operational rather than decorative.

raised.raise: Linked detail panels unfold in crisp steps instead of opening generic modal dialogs.
Errors and pending saves use physical, unmistakable status slips.

options.label: Receiving ledger
options.lineage: wholesale receiving ledgers and order stamps
options.thesis: The stockroom as a bold, modern intake ledger where every change has a clear, durable trace.
options.viewport: A full-height product ledger fills the work area, with a tall add-product slip pinned at the right and a visible activity trace for created and updated dates.
options.risk: More characterful than familiar admin software; dates must remain exceptionally easy to scan.

options.label: Tabbed reference manual
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals with acetate leaves
options.thesis: Products become a clear reference system: tabs locate categories, and an edit sheet sits visibly above the list.
options.viewport: A tab rail marks the active catalog section; product details expand as a transparent reading leaf over the row beneath.
options.case: Excellent for details and errors; slightly less immediate for rapid scanning than shelf-style rows.
options.risk: The overlay treatment needs careful contrast to preserve accessibility.

options.label: Deployable stock sheet
options.viewport: A product row deploys into a connected detail plane.
options.case: Too spatial for a list staff need to scan repeatedly.
options.kept: Crisp, linked transitions for product detail.
options.risk: Novelty can distract from the stockroom task.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, neutral data table with a familiar toolbar and modal editor.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional product table with search, filters, and an Add product button.
canonCard.risk: Highly familiar, but indistinguishable from generic admin tools.
